why: Most commands are fine: `npm test`, which maps to `node --test`, the files they name, and Checks 1, 2 and 4, whose `\"` escapes become plain quotes inside bash double quotes. Check 3 is broken by its escaping. It is wrapped in bash double quotes, so `'^#+\\s.*\\b'+f+'\\b'` reaches Node as `'^#+\s.*\b'`. In a JS string, `\s` turns into `s` and `\b` turns into a backspace character. The RegExp becomes `^#+s.*<BS>name<BS>`, which can never match a Markdown heading. So every export is reported missing and the command exits 1 even on a correct README. Also, `!new` inside double quotes would set off bash history expansion in an interactive shell. Check 3 is still valid syntax, but it doesn't do what the brief says it does, so the criterion fails.
